title: Journeys are pageviews-only, though journeys.mdx says each node is a page or an event
statement: journeys.mdx says each bar in the journey visualization represents a page or an event. The journeys query filters the session's actions to AND type = 'pageview', so of the nine event types the product ingests, eight can never appear as a node. A custom event fired between two pageviews is ingested, is queryable through the events endpoints, and is simply absent from the journey that walks straight past it.

handVerified.note: Report section 9, both halves. One session walks /start, then the custom event signup_clicked, then /middle, then /end, each 1.2 s apart so the ordering cannot be a same-second tie (see R2). CONTROL GET /events/names returns [{"eventName":"signup_clicked","count":1}], proving the event is stored and queryable. PROBE GET /journeys?steps=4 returns {"journeys":[{"path":["/start","/middle","/end"],"count":1,"percentage":100}]}. The board scenario fails at step 11 expecting the journey body to contain the event name.

source.howDecided: git log 613cd015..HEAD on both files returns nothing. At HEAD getJourneys.ts:74 still reads "AND type = 'pageview'" inside the per-session events WHERE clause, and journeys.mdx:13 still reads 'Each bar represents a page or event. Its height indicates how many users reached that point.'

local regex over all 320 issues: journey  ->  6 hits (#922, #920, #784, #770, #540, #145); the three open journeys issues are the cited ones and none is about event nodes

reevaluation: The finding stands, source untouched, still unreported, and the three open journeys issues the report cited are all unchanged and all about something else. The interesting question for a filer is which way the fix should go, and we should not presume: including eight more event types as journey nodes would change what the visualization means and could make it unreadable for a busy site, so 'the doc should say pages' is at least as likely an outcome as 'the query should include events', and both are legitimate. That makes this a report about a promise, not a demand for a feature. Severity is low, confidence in the observation is high. Because #784 is open and in the same area, cross-link it so a maintainer triaging journeys sees the whole picture at once.
notes: Report section 9 (a deliberate red; the report gives it no F id). Doc-side finding with a possible product reading. The docs live in this same repo under docs/content/docs, so there is no separate docs repo and no 'docs repo issue' route: a doc fix here is a one-line PR against rybbit-io/rybbit. Five of the ten findings (R6, R7, R8, R9, R10) are doc-side. Filing five separate doc issues would burn maintainer patience for little gain; consider one consolidated 'documentation does not match behaviour' issue listing all five with file and line, or a single PR. Present it neutrally: quote journeys.mdx:13, quote getJourneys.ts:74, show the control (the event is stored and queryable through /events/names) and the probe (it is absent from the journey), and let the maintainers choose whether the doc or the query is wrong. Cross-link #784 as an open neighbour. Do not argue for including all nine event types; autocapture types in particular (input_change, form_submit) would flood a journey, and #1031 shows the maintainers already think about how autocapture types are stored. rybbit-io/rybbit applies NO labels: all 40 most recent issues carry an empty label array, and both templates declare labels: ''. Do not add a 'Suggested labels' line here; there is no vocabulary to copy and it would only add noise. The bug template is a classic markdown template with bold headers (**Describe the bug**, **To Reproduce**, **Expected behavior**, **Screenshots**, **Desktop**, **Smartphone**, **Additional context**), not a YAML form, and no template-enforcing workflow exists, so there is no auto-close bot to trip.
